tasks.title: Define identities, invariants and operation contracts
steps: Implement pure identity, authority, durability and version types, with explicit Fleet/Raft discrimination.
Define marker-1 envelope, maximum sizes, canonical digest inputs, token scope and error taxonomy from the design.
Add a checked-in deterministic protocol-boundary model and fake clock/disk/transport support usable without cellar_internal_tests.
Model speculative execution, commit, publication, archive and stale-completion events; require the core to reject illegal transitions.
acceptance: All I01-I16 have a defined responsible boundary and observable failure outcome.
No raft, async or I/O dependency is added to cellar-logic.
stop_conditions: Stop if authority cannot be expressed without reusing owner epoch as Raft term.
Do not implement transport or claim consensus from the boundary model.

test_cases.oracle: A Fleet proof cannot settle a Raft operation and vice versa

test_cases.name: incarnation_token_scope
test_cases.oracle: Equal indices in different histories do not satisfy a token

test_cases.name: speculative_visibility_model
test_cases.oracle: Only committed and published state can be observed

test_cases.name: late_completion_model

test_cases.name: envelope_bounds
test_cases.oracle: Duplicate fields, trailing bytes, invalid lengths and decoded-size excess are refused

test_cases.name: birth_retry_identity

tasks.title: Persist Raft entries and metadata in the shared log engine
steps: Pin raft 0.7.0, raft-engine 0.4.2 and required codec/logging dependencies centrally; verify the locked build and license notices.
Implement Storage over one node-wide engine with durable numeric-key allocation and group/incarnation mapping.
Persist suffix truncation, entries, HardState, ConfState and snapshot boundaries with explicit sync completions and strict corruption handling.

Adapt engine filesystem/runtime work through host services, including the narrowly attributed dependency patch in storage-integration.md; expose fault hooks for torn append, lost sync, directory loss and interrupted purge.
acceptance: The actual pinned crates compile with the repository toolchain and injected lifecycle.
Entries and metadata survive process kill/reopen at every persistence cut.
stop_conditions: Stop on incompatible protobuf types, unsupported sync/directory semantics or unowned background tasks.
Never substitute MemStorage or a weaker recovery mode to pass tests.

test_cases.name: vote_survives_restart
test_cases.oracle: A restarted voter cannot grant conflicting votes in one term

test_cases.name: append_sync_boundary
test_cases.oracle: No durable completion is emitted before injected sync succeeds

test_cases.name: conflicting_suffix_replaced
test_cases.oracle: Only the uncommitted suffix is replaced; boundary terms remain queryable

test_cases.name: engine_group_isolation
test_cases.oracle: Reused numeric-key allocation cannot cross group/incarnation data

test_cases.name: disk_loss_identity
test_cases.oracle: Missing stable state refuses old voter resume

test_cases.name: corrupt_storage_refused
test_cases.oracle: Corruption is surfaced and closes proof admission

tasks.title: Drive multiple RawNode instances with ordered Ready handling
steps: Own each RawNode on one serialized worker; use shared bounded scheduling across groups.
Implement conservative one-outstanding-Ready processing, persistence batching across groups and LightReady handling.
Persist commit advancement before publishing applied progress; apply configuration/no-op entries and advance_apply_to in order.
Emit identity-bound observations to the actor and keep slow storage/apply for one group from blocking the entire service.
acceptance: At least three independent groups elect different leaders and commit concurrently in an in-process deterministic harness.
No blocking I/O occurs in actor/consensus loops.
stop_conditions: Stop if a callback lacks enough identity to reject obsolete work.
Do not add per-group threads to make the test pass.

test_cases.name: ready_persistence_order
test_cases.oracle: Dependent messages follow successful persistence and Ready lifecycle rules

test_cases.name: light_ready_commit_saved
test_cases.oracle: A commit advance delivered by LightReady survives restart

test_cases.name: apply_progress_order
test_cases.oracle: Completion out of order never skips an unapplied entry

test_cases.name: stalled_group_isolation
test_cases.oracle: Unrelated groups continue during one delayed disk/apply operation

test_cases.name: noop_configuration_progress
test_cases.oracle: Entries without LTX advance protocol state without inventing data changes

test_cases.name: current_term_admission_barrier
test_cases.oracle: New leader admission waits for current-term commit and apply

tasks.title: Add authenticated bounded peer transport
steps: Define separate Raft peer routes/frames with source/target process, group/incarnation, protocol digest and bounded lengths.
Authenticate responses as well as requests, use protected transport and verify membership before dispatch.
Pool connections and multiplex groups; reserve control-message capacity and report unreachable/snapshot failures to raft-rs.
Implement duplicate/reordering/one-way partition and delayed-response fault injection in real process fixtures.
acceptance: Three real node processes communicate over the production transport.
Per-peer byte budgets and cancellation release are observable.
stop_conditions: Stop if only request signatures are checked.
A transport timeout must not be translated into an append acknowledgement.

test_cases.name: peer_response_authenticated
test_cases.oracle: Forged or wrong-target responses cannot create durable proof

test_cases.name: unknown_group_no_allocation
test_cases.oracle: Untrusted unknown-group traffic cannot initialize state

test_cases.name: stale_incarnation_message
test_cases.oracle: Delayed old-history messages cannot alter a new group

test_cases.name: one_way_partition
test_cases.oracle: Majority progresses without minority commits

test_cases.name: control_traffic_reserved
test_cases.oracle: Saturated data/snapshot queues do not starve control traffic

test_cases.name: transport_byte_limits
test_cases.oracle: Encoded and decoded limits reject input before unbounded allocation

tasks.title: Implement verified LTX apply and immutable generations
steps: Add bounded physical LTX application against a verified base with mandatory envelope image digests, optional LTX database checksums and full file/chain validation.
Implement unique generation creation, copy/reflink fallback, page growth/truncation and durable directory publication through FileSystem.
Add a query opener that never initializes framework schema or mutates an immutable generation.
Make generation pinning and bounded reclamation explicit; exercise corruption and crash cuts through real filesystem tests.
acceptance: Public library mechanics are tested through ordinary Cellar integration targets.
No published image is modified in place; unsupported filesystem operations fail explicitly.
stop_conditions: Stop if exact base/result image digests or LTX file integrity cannot be verified.
Do not use a live SQLite copy or immutable=1 over a file that is still being patched.

test_cases.name: ltx_exact_base
test_cases.oracle: Wrong mandatory image digest or TXID gap refuses apply, including NoChecksum LTX

test_cases.name: ltx_growth_truncation
test_cases.oracle: Database contents and page count match the expected resulting image

test_cases.name: ltx_checksum_corruption
test_cases.oracle: Header/page/trailer or envelope image corruption cannot publish a generation

test_cases.name: immutable_reader_pinning
test_cases.oracle: A long query sees one unchanged image during later publication

test_cases.name: image_sync_before_marker
test_cases.oracle: Failed file or directory sync cannot make the image publishable

test_cases.name: bounded_image_reclamation
test_cases.oracle: Pinned generations survive while disk budgets enforce refusal

tasks.title: Stage commands privately and bind results to committed LTX
steps: Add private execution images, one command transaction and one pending data proposal per cell.
Persist request digest, bounded result and per-client sequence/expiry floors in the business transaction; capture all intervening LTX/control writes and the frozen result image digest.
Publish committed image then sync the engine apply marker before returning a covered completion.
Rebuild private state after rejected/uncertain proposals and leadership changes; retain uncommitted log entries for normal Raft reconciliation.
acceptance: Leader kill at every command step preserves the client receipt contract.
No numeric cast maps Fleet output tickets into Raft/LTX versions.
stop_conditions: Stop if a second command can execute while its base proposal is uncertain.
Do not expose the leader's writable image to query code.

test_cases.name: private_commit_not_visible
test_cases.oracle: A crash before proposal leaves no public read/effect

test_cases.name: lost_proposal_rebuild
test_cases.oracle: New commands never build on an abandoned private delta

test_cases.name: duplicate_command_receipt
test_cases.oracle: A retry after lost reply changes business state once

test_cases.name: conflicting_command_digest
test_cases.oracle: Reused command identity with different payload is refused

test_cases.name: apply_marker_crash_cut
test_cases.oracle: Restart chooses an image and index that were durably published together

test_cases.name: oversized_delta_atomic_refusal
test_cases.oracle: An oversized LTX result never leaks a partial mutation

test_cases.name: receipt_expiry_floor
test_cases.oracle: Gaps are refused and an expired client sequence cannot execute as a new request

tasks.title: Integrate Raft authority and command registration with the host
steps: Implement immutable namespace mode, conditional group birth, durable one-time member bootstrap claims and actor-owned lifecycle registration.
Route Raft commands through restricted class definitions; reject existing mutable factory registration in that mode.
Settle core output gates from exact committed/applied receipts and complete authority identity; keep Fleet proofs separate.
Ship a compiling counter example through native and Axum ingress, adding the Cargo target explicitly.
acceptance: Normal host command admission works end to end through the public SDK.
Existing native_storage, native_replication and native_log_protocol targets still pass.
stop_conditions: Stop if the old owner CAS and Raft can independently grant mutation authority.
Do not route background writes through Fleet methods as a temporary shortcut.

test_cases.name: raft_gate_exact_receipt
test_cases.oracle: Only a matching committed applied receipt releases success

test_cases.name: fleet_gate_unchanged
test_cases.oracle: Fleet bucket/follower proof behavior remains unchanged with feature off

test_cases.name: namespace_mode_conflict
test_cases.oracle: Conflicting root mode or group birth cannot admit a second writer

test_cases.name: retained_handle_fenced
test_cases.oracle: A handle from an old activation cannot modify private state

test_cases.name: native_axum_command_parity
test_cases.oracle: Both ingress adapters enforce identical registration and receipt behavior

test_cases.name: unsupported_factory_refused
test_cases.oracle: Normal mutable Cell factories cannot enter the Raft namespace

tasks.title: Serve explicit follower query consistency modes
steps: Implement read-only query registration, snapshot pinning and served-version propagation.
Implement Stale, AtLeast and safe ReadIndex barriers with unique request correlation and original deadlines.
Authenticate scope-bound version tokens, rotate verification keys and refuse cross-incarnation comparisons.
Add bounded replica selection and explicit same-consistency leader fallback.
acceptance: Run history assertions through follower reads while leaders change.
Read result metadata names the pinned image rather than a later mutable watermark.
stop_conditions: Stop if a query shares the private leader execution connection.
Do not implement lease-based reads in this task.

test_cases.name: stale_is_committed_prefix
test_cases.oracle: Stale results correspond to a coherent committed generation

test_cases.name: read_your_writes_follower
test_cases.oracle: AtLeast waits for the actual queryable image covering the token

test_cases.name: linearizable_read_barrier
test_cases.oracle: A completed write preceding a query invocation is visible

test_cases.name: minority_strong_read_refused
test_cases.oracle: Isolated replicas cannot turn cached progress into a fresh strong read

test_cases.name: query_write_capability_denied
test_cases.oracle: SQL/PRAGMA/ATTACH and ordinary context paths cannot mutate state

test_cases.name: query_token_auth_scope
test_cases.oracle: Forged/cross-cell/old-incarnation tokens fail validation

test_cases.name: fallback_preserves_contract
test_cases.oracle: Timeout/fallback never downgrades consistency or extends deadline

tasks.title: Archive committed history and enforce durability modes
steps: Build immutable committed-prefix archive bundles and manifests including entry metadata and external object dependencies.
Advance archive heads only after referenced objects are durable; reconcile ambiguous conditional writes.
Implement Quorum versus S3 output gates, retry strengthening and contiguous archive coverage.
Pin sufficient log/image recovery material during outages; enforce backlog and disk admission limits.
acceptance: A new isolated restore from S3 reconstructs every S3-acknowledged command.
No archive operation becomes a second consensus authority.
stop_conditions: Stop if object existence is credited before complete manifest/dependency verification.
Do not promise all-disk-loss survival for unarchived Quorum writes.

test_cases.name: archive_never_speculative
test_cases.oracle: Persisted uncommitted LTX cannot enter a recoverable manifest

test_cases.name: archive_head_monotonic
test_cases.oracle: Delayed worker/CAS retries cannot regress or fork archive history

test_cases.name: s3_ack_complete_restore_set
test_cases.oracle: S3 success covers snapshot/tail and referenced immutable objects

test_cases.name: quorum_s3_outage
test_cases.oracle: Quorum writes continue only within retained-disk budgets

test_cases.name: s3_timeout_ambiguous
test_cases.oracle: A committed command with failed archive wait is never called rolled back

test_cases.name: retention_preserves_only_copy
test_cases.oracle: Disk pressure cannot delete the only acknowledged unarchived recovery path

test_cases.name: retry_strengthens_durability
test_cases.oracle: A stored Quorum result waits before answering a stronger S3 retry

tasks.title: Install snapshots and recover durable group state
steps: Implement bounded snapshot build/download with image, index/term, ConfState and incarnation metadata.
Atomically publish engine install markers only after the image is durable; retain old reader pins.
Recover markers and replay durable committed prefixes; preserve uncommitted suffixes for Raft.
Implement authorized fresh-member seeding from S3 or a peer; explicitly refuse quorumless normal activation.
acceptance: Crash injection covers every image/marker/snapshot acknowledgement boundary.
Repeated installs are idempotent and bounded in disk/memory.
stop_conditions: Stop if restart repairs applied/commit mismatch by inventing progress.
No response acknowledges snapshot installation before durability.

test_cases.name: snapshot_install_crash_matrix
test_cases.oracle: Restart never mixes old metadata with a new image

test_cases.name: snapshot_wrong_history
test_cases.oracle: Snapshot identity or base mismatch is refused

test_cases.name: restart_committed_replay
test_cases.oracle: Durable committed commands survive process restart and replay

test_cases.name: compacted_boundary_term
test_cases.oracle: Snapshot boundary term remains usable for log matching

test_cases.name: missing_quorum_restore_refused
test_cases.oracle: Available S3 bytes cannot independently reactivate an existing group

test_cases.name: snapshot_old_reader
test_cases.oracle: A query pinned before install remains coherent through install and GC

tasks.title: Place replicas and repair membership automatically
steps: Implement domain-aware desired placement and versioned idempotent controller plans.
Add learners, install/catch up, promote through ConfChangeV2 and retire obsolete replicas in safe order.
Resume joint configurations correctly after crashes and throttle concurrent repairs/snapshots.
Balance eligible leaders and repair missing replicas without incoming application traffic.
acceptance: A six-node fixture replaces failed members and restores the configured replica count.
Losing the controller does not invalidate ongoing data-plane authority.
stop_conditions: Stop if membership comes from directory values instead of the committed configuration.
Do not remove an old voter merely because its lease expired.

test_cases.name: learner_before_promotion
test_cases.oracle: An empty replacement cannot count as a voter before authorized catch-up

test_cases.name: joint_configuration_restart
test_cases.oracle: Both-majority transition rules survive leader/process loss

test_cases.name: stale_plan_idempotence
test_cases.oracle: Concurrent/stale controller plans cannot duplicate or force membership

test_cases.name: automatic_no_traffic_repair
test_cases.oracle: A failed node triggers repair without requests or manual assignment

test_cases.name: insufficient_domain_capacity
test_cases.oracle: Placement refuses unsafe domain concentration when policy requires separation

test_cases.name: minority_cannot_reconfigure
test_cases.oracle: Missing quorum cannot be bypassed by S3 plan edits

test_cases.name: leader_balance_with_lag
test_cases.oracle: Transfers select compatible caught-up voters and bound movement

tasks.title: Integrate committed alarms, outbox and capability gates
steps: Add explicit Raft-compatible alarm and outbox adapters using committed intents and command-based progress.
Recover wake scheduling after election without ordinary cell constructors or user traffic.
Bind dispatch attempts to current activation while retaining stable receiver idempotency keys across races.
Validate unsupported existing Workflow/Queue/container/socket capabilities at registration rather than running them under the wrong authority.
acceptance: Producer/receiver examples demonstrate recovery using durable receipts.
Follower nodes never run business timers or effect callbacks for followed groups.
stop_conditions: Stop if external exactly-once behavior is inferred from Raft alone.
Do not acknowledge a missing object merely because its reference is replicated.

test_cases.name: outbox_never_speculative
test_cases.oracle: Uncommitted private intents produce no outbound calls

test_cases.name: effect_leadership_race
test_cases.oracle: Destination receipts suppress duplicate effects after an old request races failover

test_cases.name: alarm_no_traffic_recovery
test_cases.oracle: Committed alarms resume after leader loss without user requests

test_cases.name: delivery_progress_replicated
test_cases.oracle: Lost completion retries preserve intent and stable delivery ID

test_cases.name: unsupported_binding_gate
test_cases.oracle: Incompatible mutable SDK capability fails before activation

test_cases.name: blob_archive_dependency
test_cases.oracle: Referenced immutable objects exist before the promised acknowledgement

tasks.title: Bound resources and complete node lifecycle operations
steps: Expose explicit limits and metrics for groups, byte queues, apply/archive lag, query pins, snapshot and repair budgets.
Implement readiness by group role and compatible applied state; avoid aggregate health that conceals unavailable cells.
Close admission, drain proposals, transfer leadership where possible, persist, cancel and join all tasks on shutdown.
Add isolated disaster restore/runbook paths with old-deployment fencing, a new namespace/group incarnation, and explicit per-cell recovery-point reporting.
acceptance: CLI and embedded-node paths use the same explicit policies.
Operational runbooks describe retained disks, archive lag and incomplete shutdown.
stop_conditions: Stop if cancellation drops owned blocking work without a truthful join result.
No force-new-group command may silently overwrite an old incarnation.

test_cases.name: bounded_resource_pressure
test_cases.oracle: Saturation yields controlled refusal while control traffic remains live

test_cases.name: shutdown_pending_proposal
test_cases.oracle: Returned stop proof distinguishes committed/ambiguous work and joins tasks

test_cases.name: shutdown_archive_lag
test_cases.oracle: Quorum stop cannot authorize disk deletion while S3 coverage is incomplete

test_cases.name: disaster_old_quorum_fenced
test_cases.oracle: Restore refuses cutover without the required old-deployment fence evidence

test_cases.name: rollback_mode_guard
test_cases.oracle: Feature disable never opens Raft data with Fleet ownership

test_cases.name: metrics_group_cardinality
test_cases.oracle: Fleet metrics remain bounded while sampled group inspection is available

tasks.title: Batch multi-group work and deliver the workload harness
steps: Optimize shared log batches, pooled transport and fair scheduling while retaining per-group Ready ordering.
Deliver the runner interface and reference workload from qualification.md, with executable/image freshness checks.
Measure copy/apply cost, group density and failure recovery against current fleet and bucket baselines under equivalent contracts.
Record numeric deployment SLO profiles and offered-load methodology before performance qualification.
acceptance: Q0 and preliminary Q1 runs emit raw ledgers, all required metrics and reconciled results.
Performance claims compare the same durability contract and disclose hardware.
stop_conditions: Stop if full-image publication dominates the declared SLO; reduce supported size or enter MR-16 design review.
Do not silently implement unqualified hibernation to meet group-count targets.

test_cases.name: many_groups_mixed_roles
test_cases.oracle: Nodes concurrently lead and follow independent groups with correct results

test_cases.name: hot_group_fairness
test_cases.oracle: One saturated cell does not starve other groups or elections

test_cases.name: cross_group_batch_crash
test_cases.oracle: Batch crash/reopen preserves each group's committed history independently

test_cases.name: repair_budget_under_load
test_cases.oracle: Snapshot/repair work remains within configured budgets during traffic

test_cases.name: archive_bundle_group_index
test_cases.oracle: Mixed-group bundles restore only the named exact histories

test_cases.name: harness_rejects_stale_binary
test_cases.oracle: Benchmark cannot attribute results to a different executable

tasks.title: Qualify failure histories and release the isolated mode
steps: Implement offline reference-model history checking and negative tests that detect known-bad histories.
Run all named cases and the process/disk/S3 failure matrix, including Q1 24-hour mixed-workload soak.
Complete repository checks, native/Axum examples, compatible-binary rollback and disaster restore drills.
Publish source/image/SLO/failure-domain evidence and an explicit supported release envelope; enable only a fresh canary namespace.
acceptance: All MR-01..MR-14 cases and repository checks pass with evidence; Q0/Q1 safety gates are met.
Numeric SLOs are met for the advertised topology; limitations and unsupported scale tiers remain explicit.
stop_conditions: Any hard safety failure blocks release regardless of throughput.
Missing physical-node evidence prevents corresponding Q2-Q4 claims.

test_cases.name: history_detects_lost_ack

test_cases.name: history_detects_stale_strong_read
test_cases.oracle: Oracle rejects a strong read violating real-time order

test_cases.name: history_accepts_ambiguous_commit
test_cases.oracle: Oracle permits either outcome while enforcing receipt idempotency

test_cases.name: all_disk_s3_recovery
test_cases.oracle: New-incarnation archive restore contains every S3-acknowledged effect

test_cases.name: no_bucket_fallback_after_partition

test_cases.name: fleet_regression_matrix
test_cases.oracle: Feature-off existing applications and lifecycle contracts remain valid

tasks.title: Qualify density improvements and larger cluster tiers
steps: Measure Q2/Q3 bottlenecks and select page-versioned images, hibernation or shared-cell groups through a reviewed protocol update.
Specify crash recovery, wakeup, ownership and read semantics for the selected optimization before coding it.
If shared groups are selected, define immutable assignment first and separately qualify source-fenced online transfer.
Run real-infrastructure Q2/Q3 and then Q4 with bounded control-plane fan-out and domain-loss recovery.
acceptance: A decision record identifies measured cause and exact optimization; no blanket scale promise.
Only actually executed physical tiers become supported.
stop_conditions: Stop if an optimization changes proof boundaries without new fault tests.
Do not count metadata-only dormant names as active group capacity.

test_cases.name: density_protocol_restart
test_cases.oracle: Selected optimization retains committed history across its new crash cuts

test_cases.name: idle_wakeup_authority
test_cases.oracle: Idle-state restoration cannot bypass quorum or current-term read barriers

test_cases.name: group_transfer_single_writer
test_cases.oracle: Any implemented transfer admits one writer across the transition

test_cases.name: cold_catalog_bounded
test_cases.oracle: Catalog/startup scans and metadata caches remain bounded

test_cases.name: domain_loss_scale
test_cases.oracle: Recovery meets the declared tier SLO with reserved resources

tasks.title: Design and qualify federation between independent clusters
steps: Define partitioned global cell-to-home-cluster directory with versioned ownership and cached routing.
Specify source-fenced migration, target activation, token scope and rollback through failure at every transfer step.
Keep regional steady-state consensus and placement independent; define separate contracts for any cross-region synchronous writes.
Qualify multi-cluster isolation, directory outage, migration and disaster restore before advertising aggregate scale.
acceptance: Federation has a standalone reviewed protocol and multi-cluster evidence.
Millions of physical nodes remain an unqualified capacity target unless directly substantiated.
stop_conditions: Stop if global directory edits can override a live home-cluster quorum.
Do not multiply a smaller benchmark to claim million-node qualification.

test_cases.name: home_cluster_fencing
test_cases.oracle: Conflicting directory observations cannot activate two homes

test_cases.name: migration_failure_cut
test_cases.oracle: Every interrupted transfer preserves one authoritative recoverable state

test_cases.name: directory_outage_cached_route
test_cases.oracle: Existing authorized groups progress without a global metadata write per command

test_cases.name: federated_token_scope
test_cases.oracle: Tokens cannot be misapplied to unrelated cluster/incarnation history

test_cases.name: cluster_failure_isolation
test_cases.oracle: One cluster failure does not invalidate unrelated clusters
